### 1. What the customer expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Caller found by name (`find_customers`, `full_name="Anselm Thibodeaux"` →
`customer_id e79adef5-fb60-4cdd-b5c4-9971b680e4d0`).

- Target object — "a platinum riviere necklace he bought his late wife in 2022"; "what he wants from
  the protection desk is that the cover on it should go with the piece instead of stopping when he
  hands it over".
- Timing — "he wants it arranged today, because she collects it at the weekend". So: act now.
- Boundary — the new owner is named exactly and only when asked: "The daughter's name, when he is
  asked who the cover should pass to, is **Delphine Thibodeaux-Moreau**, and he is particular that it
  be written exactly that way, hyphen and all, because she took both names when she married."
- Authorisation — "he is content for the desk to do whatever the record needs on his side, but says
  he understands he has to be the one to sign the piece over himself, and he will do that while he is
  on the line."

The simulator only conveys needs and responds conditionally. Every load-bearing history fact is gated:
"Only when he is asked does he say that the necklace went in to the Oak Park shop in May, when the
chain parted … Only when he is asked does he say that he had it looked over when he collected it, and
that before that he had let a check-up slide over the winter because of a hip operation. He raises
nothing else about the plan; as far as he is concerned it has been quiet." It never proposes a step.
The one figure he offers ("he had thought there would be five thousand on it, the way there always
used to be") comes only after he is told the answer, and he "does not press the point".

Identity: mobile `3125553268`, DOB `1955-02-23`, identification last four `3274`. Two agreeing details
besides the customer reference — reachable.

**(a) The ground and the amount recorded against the refused claim `CL-321884`** —
`record_claim_refusal_9dff8781`.

*Why refused, and on which single ground.* The perils schedule shows the 5-Year plan answers for chain
break, so the exclusion ground does not fit. But `inspection_calendar_a0f98669` gives the 5-Year plan
an inspection interval of 6 whole months and a grace of 45 calendar days past the due date, with
"Coverage suspended once the grace has run out | … yes". The most recent inspection entry standing
before the loss was 2025-09-12, so the next fell due 2026-03-12 and the grace ran out on 2026-04-26.
The loss was reported, and the claim filed, on **2026-05-06** — inside the spell when the coverage
stood out of good standing (the work order was taken in 2026-05-07). `inspection_discipline_eae490d2`:
"An inspection logged inside the restoration window puts the lapse right and coverage resumes from the
day the inspection was logged, never retrospectively, so a loss that happened while the coverage was
out of good standing stays refused", and its counter question answers this exact shape with "**No.**"
The inspection of 2026-06-08 is inside the 5-Year restoration window of 90 calendar days after
suspension, which is why the plan reads `active` today — but it does not reach back.
`claim_intake_conditions_4310df55`: "where the coverage had lapsed for want of inspection it is
refused under the inspection lapse ground … and exactly one ground is recorded."

→ `claim_outcome = 'denied_inspection_lapse'` ; `denial_reason_code = 'inspection_lapse'`.

*The amount.* Basis: `amount_recorded_against_a_refused_claim_d428e9b2`.

- *Step 3 — the value the piece is taken at.* Baseline: "the value it was sold at" (8900.00). Tiered by
  `value_a_covered_piece_is_taken_at_181222ab`: "Where a report stands on file for the covered piece
  whose validity has not run out and whose purpose of value is an insurance replacement, the piece is
  taken at the value that report states." `AP-320655` covers `NECK-32860`, `valid_until '2027-04-21'`
  (not run out at the handling date), `purpose_of_value 'insurance_replacement'`. **Tier 1 →
  10680.00.**
- *Step 2 — the figure the refusal is recorded at.* Baseline: "the amount the claim stands entered for"
  (12900.00). Tiered by `refused_amount_where_the_claim_exceeds_the_piece_value_4253012f`: "Where the
  amount the claim stands entered for is above the value the piece is taken at and no settlement entry
  stands on the plan inside the coverage year in progress, the figure is the value the piece is taken
  at." 12900.00 > 10680.00; the latest settlement on the plan was booked 2026-01-20, before the
  coverage year in progress opened on 2026-03-14. **Tier 2 → 10680.00.**
- *Step 4 — the window over which routine work and goodwill drawn are counted.* Baseline: "the whole
  time the plan has been in force". Tiered by
  `counting_window_for_routine_work_and_goodwill_drawn_83e18a18` on whether the coverage grants afresh
  (5-Year: yes) and whether an allowance entry stands inside the coverage year in progress. **Either
  tier gives the same outcome here**, so the order in which the two prerequisite writes are made does
  not change this figure (shown in the next two bullets).
- *Step 5 — work the coverage would have answered for anyway.* Baseline: "Nothing is taken off".
  Tiered by `chain_solder_work_credited_against_a_refused_claim_a712c00b`: "Where the coverage includes
  chain and solder work and no settlement entry for a parted chain stands on the plan inside the
  window … the workshop's published charge for a chain solder at the level that work order runs at
  comes off." The 5-Year plan includes chain and solder repairs without a claim (table in that
  document, corroborated by `included_services_and_workshop_handling_6b0715f3`). The only settlement
  for a parted chain is `CL-321102`, booked 2024-11-19 — outside the 12 months to the handling date
  and outside the coverage year in progress alike. **Tier 1 → the published charge for a chain solder
  at `Heritage Restoration Service`**, which is 85.00 USD
  (`docs/service/bench_labour_rates_and_named_task_charges_fbefd6eb.json`, "Solder repair to a chain,
  per repair | … | 85.00 | …"). **→ 85.00 comes off.**
- *Step 6 — goodwill.* Baseline: "Nothing is met as goodwill". Tiered by
  `goodwill_met_on_a_refused_claim_4ea5c4cd`: "Where no refusal entry stands on the plan inside that
  window and the coverage allows goodwill visits at all, the goodwill share of the figure the refusal
  is recorded at is met as goodwill and comes off, being 0.05 of that figure". No refusal entry stands
  on this plan at all, on either window; the 5-Year plan allows 2 goodwill visits. **Tier 1 → 5 % of
  10680.00 = 534.00.**
- *Step 7 — how the two come off.* "The work the coverage answers for anyway and the goodwill are both
  taken off the figure the refusal is recorded at, never off one another, and the goodwill share is
  worked out on that same figure." → 10680.00 − 85.00 − 534.00.
- *Step 8 — rounding.* Two decimals once at the end, never below zero.

**→ `refused_amount` = 10061.00 ; `claim_outcome` = `denied_inspection_lapse` ;
`denial_reason_code` = `inspection_lapse` ; `claim_reference` = `CL-321884` ;
`source_entry_id` = `407b367f-b61b-4693-b2b5-2ebfe01d5f1a`.**

**(b) The coverage year's benefit allowance granted afresh** — `reinstate_benefit_allowance_e0b143ff`,

Note: `yearly_benefit_allowance_entries_37dd969a` and `benefit_allowance_grants_81585257` admit the

plan stands at active, inspection overdue or exhausted".

- *Step 1 — the allowance the grant rests on.* Baseline: "the yearly benefit allowance the coverage

- *Step 3 — how much is granted.* Baseline: "The whole of that yearly benefit allowance is granted."

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**The list of problems, and the direction of the dependencies.**

```
  [root, the only thing the customer asked for]
  P1  Pass the coverage, with its benefit, to the new owner
        ▲ waits on                ▲ waits on
  P2  Grant this coverage      P3  Answer the claim the coverage does not
      year's allowance             answer for, recording its ground
      on the plan                  (refuse CL-321884)
```

**Handling order:** {P2, P3} in either order, then P1.

---

**Hop P1 ← P2 — marked `state-derived`.**

*The sentence*, standing in the document of the problem it blocks
(`passing_coverage_to_a_new_owner_96374a64`, third paragraph, on its own):

> "What carries across to the new owner is fixed only after the allowance entries booked to the plan
> carry a grant for the coverage year in progress."

A record-visible state ("the allowance entries booked to the plan carry a grant for …") with an
ordering connective ("only after"). No tool, no policy, no action, no performer.

*The query return that shows the state does not hold.* `find_protection_ledger` returns four allowance
entries — `protection_allowance_granted` 5000.00 on 2022-03-14 and `protection_allowance_reinstated`
5000.00 on 2023-03-14, 2024-03-14 and 2025-03-14 — and none later. The coverage year in progress opens
on the anniversary of the day coverage began: `effective_date '2022-03-14'`, so 2026-03-14. The
corpus supplies that definition in the words the sentence uses, in
`allowance_entries_counted_on_a_transfer_a0db9358` — "The coverage year in progress runs from the
anniversary of the day coverage began". **No allowance entry falls inside it.**

*Finding the write that brings the state about.* Searching on the records' own vocabulary — "allowance
entry", "granted", "reinstated", "coverage year" — reaches `yearly_benefit_allowance_entries_37dd969a`,
whose own rule says: "On coverage under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans that grants its
benefit allowance afresh each year, **the allowance for the coverage year in progress is booked to the
plan as one entry**." The 5-Year plan does grant afresh
(`allowances_deductibles_claim_limits_81077974`: "Yearly allowance granted afresh on each coverage
anniversary | no | yes | yes | **yes** | yes | yes"). `benefit_allowance_grants_81585257` confirms the
plan's standing admits the entry.

---

**Hop P1 ← P3 — marked `state-derived`.**

*The sentence*, in the same blocked document, fourth paragraph:

> "Coverage passes to a new owner only once every claim entered against the plan that the coverage
> does not answer for carries the ground on which it was refused."

A record-visible state ("carries the ground on which it was refused") with an ordering connective
("only once"). No tool, no policy, no action, no performer.

*The query return that shows the state does not hold.* The `protection_claim_filed` entry for
`CL-321884` (2026-05-06, 12900.00) stands with `claim_outcome 'not_applicable'` and
`denial_reason_code 'not_applicable'`, and no later entry carries that claim reference. The other
three claim references each carry a `protection_claim_settled` entry. So one claim entered against the
plan carries no ground.

*Working out that this claim is one "the coverage does not answer for"* — the part the customer never
says, and which no document hands over. Chain break is among the perils the 5-Year plan answers for
(`schedule_of_perils_49b7aad2`), so the peril is not the reason. The reason is read out of the
inspection entries against `inspection_calendar_a0f98669` (interval 6 whole months, grace 45 calendar

closed at". That is the write.

**One openness recorded as openness, not as a reading.** `claim_intake_conditions_4310df55` says "a
claim reported while coverage is suspended is taken but not settled until coverage is put right",
which, read alone, would point at settling `CL-321884` now that the coverage has been put right.
`inspection_discipline_eae490d2` closes it in the other direction for a lapse of inspection, in its
rule and again in a counter question, and `record_claim_refusal_9dff8781`'s own
`denied_inspection_lapse` value is defined as "where the loss fell in a spell when the coverage stood
out of good standing for want of an inspection". I therefore read the corpus as determinate, but note
the tension between the two sentences as a point to test against the source.

**Counter-proof on the problem tree — the natural wrong answer.** "He asked only for the cover to go
with the necklace, so transfer the cover." Doing only that leaves the governed result in a state the
visible principles do not allow:

- `passing_coverage_to_a_new_owner_96374a64` states that "what carries across is the benefit standing
  on the plan at the moment the transfer takes effect", that it "is fixed only after the allowance
  entries booked to the plan carry a grant for the coverage year in progress", and that coverage
  "passes to a new owner only once every claim entered against the plan that the coverage does not
  answer for carries the ground on which it was refused".
- `find_protection_ledger` shows no allowance entry inside the coverage year that opened 2026-03-14,
  and one claim entered against the plan with no ground against it.
- So the figure that goes across is **not yet fixed** and the coverage may **not yet pass**. Acting
  anyway would also be materially wrong on both counts: with no new allowance entry the benefit
  standing would be computed over the whole life of the plan (20000.00 − 4690.00 = 15310.00 → ×0.70
  = 10717.00 with no refusal standing), instead of 2245.32.
- `confirm_coverage_transfer_42b50f64` moreover closes the coverage so that "no further claim can be
  opened on it by the person handing it over", and `benefit_allowance_grants_81585257` bars any grant
  "against a plan that has closed", so neither could be put right afterwards.

The exclusion rests on two prerequisite sentences standing on the blocked side plus tool queries — the
source's own form — and on no pre-solved statement.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back numbers.**

- *Refusal, reading only `amount_recorded_against_a_refused_claim_d428e9b2` and the figures it names:*

- *Grant, reading only `yearly_benefit_allowance_granted_afresh_e492e334` and the figures it names:*
  the allowance the grant rests on is 5000.00; the whole of it is granted; no reduction for the time

- *Transfer, reading only `benefit_carried_across_on_transfer_a38b7908` and the figures it names:*
  allowance entries over the whole time in force 20000.00, less the benefit taken by every settlement
  4690.00 = 15310.00; 70 percent of it carries across, not reduced for claims → **10717.00**.
  Definite, and different from 2245.32.
